From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: TalentOps <talentops@acme-talent.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Coverage plan: temporary swap & freeze-exception for Eng IC (PR impact)

Team —

Quick context: during the upcoming performance review window (Jul 5–23) we have one senior IC (E-4) on the infra team who is taking an approved 6-week sabbatical starting Jul 6. That headcount was not in the FY plan for a backfill this quarter due to the hiring freeze. The infra team is critical to our low-latency serving work and the timing intersects with an internal rollout that must keep latency SLAs.

I put together two scenarios (attached) balancing risk vs. cost:
- Scenario A: temporary assignment of a senior SRE from Platform for 6 weeks (rotation, partial overlap, no net new HC).
- Scenario B: one-time freeze-exception to post a 3-month contractor backfill (cost ~ $55k) to preserve throughput during reviews.

Asks:
1) Can Marcus + Laura review attached scenarios and confirm which option preserves launch timelines (or suggest alternatives)?
2) Karthik, if we go with B, can you approve a one-time freeze-exception and fast-track procurement?
3) Monica, can your team absorb 25% of the on-call load if we use option A?

I attached a short scenario workbook and an org chart. Short meeting to decide tomorrow morning would be ideal.

Attachments: [hc-scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)], [org-chart.pdf (PDF, 180KB)]

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear summary, Soojin. I reviewed the workbook and have two immediate notes:

- Scenario A reduces hiring cost but increases cross-team risk; Platform is already stretched in July and the SRE rotation will drop our feature engineering throughput by ~15%.
- Scenario B keeps throughput but requires procurement + security sign-off for contractor access; that typically takes 7–10 business days.

My recommendation: pursue Scenario B but prepare Plan A as the fallback. If Karthik can greenlight the freeze-exception today we can start procurement and request expedited onboarding from TalentOps.

Action items:
- Karthik: approval for freeze-exception + $60k budget envelope
- Soojin: confirm firewall/VPN exceptions for contractor in the procurement request (sensitive infra access)
- Monica: confirm if your team can commit 25% on-call coverage as contingency

Laura Bennett
VP, Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference

Agree with Laura — B is safer for SLA and external commitments (NimbusAI integration). Quick notes from the infra-runbook review:
- The three highest-risk tasks during the sabbatical are: nightly KV compaction, rolling restart cadence, and the canary gating pipeline.
- Contractor must be given scoped service account with limited write capability to prod; full admin access is unacceptable.

Estimated impact if we choose A (rotation):
- 15% longer incident time-to-resolve (MTTR) for the 6-week period
- ~10% hit to planned delivery for feature flags tied to rollout

I'm attaching a short runbook excerpt that highlights gating steps. If we go B, Laura — please add the $60k to the approval. If we go A, Monica — we'll need the schedule matrix for the rotation (start/end dates).

- Soojin/Michael (Ops) confirming the minimal IAM/service-account scope for the contractor before onboarding
